title: Module quiz: Keeping what matters in long conversations

blocks.text: Questions on what this page has just taught. Choose one answer for each.

questions.stem: Scenario S1, customer support resolution agent. A customer returns after nine days. The facts block says the parcel is out for delivery, a state that the team treats as stale after a few hours. What should the agent do before replying?

options.text: Answer from the block, because stored facts outrank guesses
options.says: Ruled out because "a stale fact is a guess with a date on it".

options.text: Ask the customer what the status was when they last looked
options.says: Ruled out because the remedy is to read the value again "from the system of record", not to ask the customer to recall it.

options.text: Read the value again from the order system and say which date applies
options.says: A fact past its freshness limit is read again from the system of record, and the agent states the date it is going by.

options.text: Discard every stored fact and rebuild the case from the customer's messages
options.says: Ruled out because the facts are valid until their limit, and the block is how the numbers survive: "the case facts block carries the numbers".

questions.stem: Scenario S3, multi-agent research system. A synthesis agent receives forty findings from subagents as one long text, and its report leaves out findings from the middle of that text. Which change fits best?

options.text: Ask each subagent for longer explanations so that every finding takes more room
options.says: Ruled out because "the middle is where findings go missing", and longer text makes the middle longer.

options.text: Open with a short digest of key points, then group detail under headers
options.says: Key findings go first under a header, with the detail under explicit headers.

options.text: Send the same forty findings twice so that each one appears in two places
options.says: Ruled out because the guide's remedy is placement: "Put the key findings and the case facts at the beginning of the aggregated input".

options.text: Sort the findings alphabetically before they are joined into the input
options.says: Ruled out because ordering by name changes nothing about where a finding sits: "Organise the detail under explicit headers".

questions.stem: Scenario S1, customer support resolution agent. A customer raises a late parcel and a billing error in one chat, each carrying a different sum, and later returns to the parcel. The agent mixes the sums. Which structure fits?

options.text: A single running total of the sums that spans both matters at once
options.says: Ruled out because "each issue has its own entry in the block, so that two refunds in one conversation never share an amount".

options.text: One summary sentence that covers both matters and their sums
options.says: Ruled out because "A reader of the summary cannot tell that anything was lost".

options.text: Dropping the first matter's data as soon as the second matter begins
options.says: Ruled out because "no issue's entry is dropped until the case closes".

options.text: A separate entry per matter with figures and dates, kept to closure
options.says: Each matter has its own entry, and no entry is dropped until the case closes.
